activity.notes: Lee Kuan Yew was sworn in as Singapore's first Prime Minister on 5 June 1959 and continuously held the office through Singapore's self-government, merger with Malaysia, separation and independence, until 27 November 1990. The constitutional status of Singapore changed during his tenure, but the Singapore premiership itself remained continuous; ATLAS therefore models one continuous Prime Minister Activity rather than splitting the same office at 1963 or 1965. He became Senior Minister on 28 November 1990, which is outside the scope of this primary registration Activity.

sources.title: Mr LEE Kuan Yew - Past Prime Ministers
sources.citation_text: The Prime Minister's Office Singapore lists Lee Kuan Yew's office-holding appointment as Prime Minister from 5 June 1959 to 27 November 1990, followed by appointment as Senior Minister on 28 November 1990.

sources.title: Law of the Land
sources.citation_text: The National Library Board explains that the 1958 constitutional order created the office of Prime Minister and that Lee Kuan Yew was sworn in as Singapore's first Prime Minister on 5 June 1959 after the May 1959 election.

sources.title: Lee Kuan Yew
sources.citation_text: The National Library Board identifies Lee Kuan Yew as Singapore's first prime minister, serving from 1959 to 1990.
